scenario: Hindsight (post-hoc) — the day as raced: a 44-man escape, a four-up finish, the GC group at 4:12
note: Post-race reconstruction, NOT a prediction — run with --no-log and never written to prediction_log. Forty-four riders went clear in a frantic opening and were given seven minutes; on the Pandera the escape came down to Buitrago, Brenner, Cristian Rodriguez and Sosa, Buitrago attacked on the steepest section, Brenner came back to him as the road eased and passed him metres from the line to win by a second, Rodriguez 11 seconds back and Sosa 14. The first GC riders — Mas and Gall together — were 21st and 22nd at 4:12, with Roglic at 4:37, Carapaz at 4:43, Kuss at 5:09, Onley and Omrzel at 5:27 and Skjelmose at 5:29. References are Grand Tour mountain stages won from an escape by a two- or three-up finish with the GC group minutes behind (winner groups of 2-3, tiny margins, under 15% of the field inside two minutes): Zana's Giro 2023 stage 18 at Val di Zoldo, Kämna's Etna stage at the Giro 2022, Kwiatkowski's TdF 2020 stage 18, van Garderen's Giro 2017 stage 18 at Ortisei and Pantano's TdF 2016 stage 15 at Culoz — a set disjoint from every prior board on this race. The question, as at Valdelinares and Calar Alto: does a profile built from days the escape actually won recover Brenner (#22-50 on the morning boards) or Sosa (#33-42), or is this the break-membership wall again?
